title: Oh captain, our captain: Ars staff remembers Patrick Stewart
gist: Ars Technica staff remember Sir Patrick Stewart, best known as Star Trek: TNG's Captain Jean-Luc Picard and X-Men's Professor Charles Xavier, who died at 86 at his Los Angeles home after Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. The piece traces his move from Royal Shakespeare Company stage actor to sci-fi icon. Staff recall his range, his comedy and his COVID-era Shakespeare sonnet readings.

insights.claim: Patrick Stewart died at 86 at his Los Angeles home following a brief journey with Alzheimer's Disease and Lewy Body Dementia. His family asked that memorial gifts go to the Johns Hopkins Alzheimer's Disease Research Center Fund and the Alzheimer's Foundation of America Caregiver Resources.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
entities: Johns Hopkins Alzheimer's Disease Research Center Fund
insights.so_what: His death puts a public spotlight on dementia research and caregiver charities.

themes.theme: Career path from stage to sci-fi

insights.claim: Stewart's big break came in his late 40s. A TV producer developing TNG heard him lecture on Shakespeare at UCLA and pushed him for captain of the Enterprise-D, and his audition won over a reluctant Gene Roddenberry.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Casting a classical stage actor as Picard gave the franchise its gravitas.
insights.quote: Creator Gene Roddenberry wasn’t initially keen on the choice, but Stewart’s audition changed his mind.

insights.claim: Ian McKellen recalls warning Stewart that taking the Star Trek offer risked his UK stage career and getting lost in Hollywood for years. Stewart took the risk anyway.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: The career bet against conventional advice paid off.

insights.claim: After TNG ended in 1994, Stewart played Professor Charles Xavier in 2000's X-Men and returned to the role in six more films, with his final appearance coming in Avengers: Doomsday in December.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A posthumous release is still ahead.
insights.quote: Stewart’s final appearance as Charles Xavier will be in Avengers: Doomsday in December.

insights.claim: Stewart was a serious actor who never took himself too seriously. He moved between Shakespeare, Ibsen and Beckett and comedy appearances on Saturday Night Live, The Daily Show, Sesame Street and Ricky Gervais' Extras.

insights.so_what: His broad range kept him popular well beyond Trek.

themes.theme: Picard as a model of leadership

insights.claim: Eric Berger argues that Picard's warmth, decency, honesty and intellectualism stand in contrast with current leadership in the US and elsewhere, which regularly shows the opposite. That contrast is why people miss the character.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Fictional leadership ideals now carry political weight with fans.
insights.quote: At a time when our leadership in the United States, and many other countries around the world, regularly showcases the opposite of these characteristics
